nirāmisasutta: [Nirāmisa+sutta.(nirā-mipasutra-saṃ)]  CL=7 The Nirāmisa Sutta explains how the Buddha taught the bhikkhus about the nature of happiness (sukha) and its relationship to attachment (kilesā āmisa). The happiness (sukha) that arises in the consciousness of a bhikkhu who enters the first and second jhāna is associated with vimokkha (liberation) but can still be influenced by kilesā āmisa (attachments rooted in defilements). This includes forms of joy (pīti), happiness (sukha), and equanimity (upekkhā) connected to sensual pleasures (kāmaguṇa). In contrast, a bhikkhu who enters the fourth jhāna experiences vimokkha related to consciousness (citta vimokkha), free from kilesā āmisa. In this state, there is joy (pīti), happiness (sukha), and equanimity (upekkhā) untainted by attachment.
